record.title: LLM-PowerTrace reports time-resolved GPU power data for AI compute
record.summary: An Oct. 28 arXiv preprint introduces LLM-PowerTrace, a reported collection of GPU power traces across fine-tuning and serving. The authors describe 1,788 fine-tuning runs and 405 inference runs on NVIDIA L40S, A100, H100 and H200 GPUs, with nominal 100 ms device telemetry, and report fitted mean-power errors in the low single digits on evaluated held-out regimes. They say the complete dataset will be released upon acceptance; the currently described explorer exposes selected reference traces. The preprint does not establish independent reproduction, facility-level energy measurement or grid effects.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report a collection comprising 1,788 fine-tuning runs and 405 serving runs across NVIDIA L40S, A100, H100 and H200 GPUs, with nominal 100 ms device power telemetry and run configuration/event metadata.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For the measured configurations, the authors report fitted power estimates with median mean-node-power error of about 2.7% and held-out errors generally between 1.3% and 6.1%. These are paper-reported results, not independently reproduced here.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors describe a public explorer containing selected reference traces, while stating that the complete dataset will be released upon acceptance. The full raw collection was not inspected in this review.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint does not establish independent reproduction, generalization beyond its measured GPUs and workloads, facility-level electricity use, grid impact, or a validated method for translating device traces into site energy.

evidence_gaps.description: The complete raw trace dataset is stated to be forthcoming upon acceptance; only selected public reference traces are described in the accessible explorer. The anonymous code endpoint returned HTTP 403 during this review.
No independent reproduction of the reported model fits or data-collection results was found or performed.
The reported traces are GPU-device measurements in selected training and serving configurations; server power, cooling, facility overhead and grid response are not measured.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported traces and power-model fits hold, temporally resolved measurements across training and serving workloads could improve GPU energy accounting and AI-compute scheduling. The study is bounded to selected NVIDIA GPUs and software/workload regimes, has open measurement and external-validation questions, and does not establish facility or grid-level effects.
limitations: This is an author-reported arXiv preprint and has not been independently reproduced in this review.
The paper states the full dataset will be released upon acceptance; the full raw collection was unavailable for inspection here.
Reported fit errors apply to evaluated configurations; the paper describes larger errors for ramp transients and an out-of-family model.
GPU-device traces do not establish server/facility electricity use, cooling overhead, or grid-level effects.
brief.summary: An Oct. 28 arXiv preprint introduces LLM-PowerTrace, a reported collection of GPU power traces across fine-tuning and serving. The authors describe 1,788 fine-tuning runs and 405 inference runs on NVIDIA L40S, A100, H100 and H200 GPUs, with nominal 100 ms device telemetry, and report fitted mean-power errors in the low single digits on evaluated held-out regimes. They say the complete dataset will be released upon acceptance; the currently described explorer exposes selected reference traces. The preprint does not establish independent reproduction, facility-level energy measurement or grid effects.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report 1,788 fine-tuning and 405 serving runs across four NVIDIA GPU families, nominal 100 ms telemetry, median mean-node-power fit error around 2.7%, and held-out errors of 1.3–6.1% in evaluated regimes. These values are source-reported and should not be extrapolated beyond the measured setups.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible arXiv preprint presents the dataset design and reported results. The full dataset was not available for inspection and no independent measurements or reproduction were conducted.
technical.mechanism: The paper records time-aligned GPU telemetry during selected fine-tuning and vLLM serving runs and fits models relating workload/configuration features to mean GPU-node power. It proposes extensions to power-aware compute scheduling; this review did not reproduce its collection or modeling pipeline.
technical.regime: Selected NVIDIA L40S/A100/H100/H200 fine-tuning and inference workloads, including vLLM serving; nominal 100 ms GPU power telemetry. The paper identifies ramp transients and out-of-family models as limitations. It does not measure complete server or facility power.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper reports its fitted estimates against measured power on its held-out data. No independent baseline model or external facility-meter comparison was inspected in this review.

brief.title: LLM-PowerTrace reports time-resolved GPU power data for AI compute
brief.why_it_matters: Time-resolved power traces could improve estimates of accelerator energy use and help evaluate workload scheduling if the reported coverage and fit quality hold. The evidence concerns selected GPU devices and software/workload regimes, and does not establish server/facility energy or grid-level consequences.
